# Wester Ross Biosphere

Dramatic mountains, rich biodiversity and a strong connection between people and the land are at the heart of this biosphere.

## At a glance

- Nature & outdoors:
5,200 square kilometres of spectacular mountains, forests, waterfalls, seascapes and lochs

- Wildlife:
White-tailed eagles, otters, seals, whales, pine martens, deer and red squirrels

- Towns & villages:
Achiltibuie, Applecross, Aultbea, Dornie, Gairloch, Kinlochewe, Kyle of Lochalsh, Laide, Lochcarron, Plockton, Poolewe, Shieldaig, Torridon, Ullapool


Map of Scotland

## About the biosphere

Stretching across 5,200 square km in Wester Ross and Lochalsh, the Wester Ross Biosphere is one of the most scenic and most sparsely populated areas of the UK. Ancient Caledonian pine forests, towering mountains and coastlines teeming with wildlife sit alongside centuries-old crofting communities. Gaelic heritage plays an important role here, from place names and traditions to the concept of ‘dùthchas’ – a deep sense of belonging between people and the land they live in.

Walk scenic mountain trails, spot native wildlife, uncover rich and sometimes surprising stories in museums and heritage sites, and experience a living landscape where communities, culture and nature continue to thrive side by side.

## Highlights in Wester Ross

Discover the experiences that bring the Wester Ross Biosphere to life, from guided walks and wildlife encounters on land and sea to local history, Gaelic heritage and traditions celebrated by its communities.

### Walking

From the ancient Caledonian pine forests of Beinn Eighe to the Falls of Measach plunging into Corrieshalloch Gorge, guided walks bring the landscapes, wildlife and stories of the biosphere to life.

[Find your local guide to the biosphere](https://www.visitwester-ross.com/see-and-do/guided-walks/)

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2023/02/01/beinn-eighe)

Beinn Eighe

### Traditions

Gaelic heritage and traditions remain an important part of life in the Wester Ross Biosphere. Join a ceilidh in Poolewe, enjoy a Gaelic lunch at Gairloch Museum, or discover crofting traditions at Balmacara Estate and Duirinish.

[Find out more about crofting culture at Balmacara Estate](https://www.nts.org.uk/visit/places/balmacara-estate/highlights/the-crofting-landscape)

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2026/10/01/duirinish-crofting-village)

Duirinish crofting village

### Museums

Discover the stories of the Wester Ross Biosphere in its local museums. Explore crofting heritage at Gairloch Museum, maritime history in Ullapool or visit the Arctic Convoy Museum in Aultbea to uncover Loch Ewe's role in a daring WWII operation.

[Discover the rich history of the region](https://www.gairlochmuseum.org/)

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2026/10/01/gairloch-museum)

Gairloch Museum

### Gardens & woodland

Discover a gentler side to the biosphere at Attadale, Inverewe, and Lael Forest, or explore the restored Victorian arboretum at Leckmelm, where exotic plants thrive in the mild west coast climate.

[Find more information about forests and woodland in the biosphere \| PDF 2MB](https://www.wrb.scot/userfiles/file/Natural_Heritage/Forest-and-Woodland.pdf)

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2022/11/16/attadale-gardens-in-wester-ross)

Attadale Gardens

## Sustainable local businesses

Explore a range of responsible businesses, activities and experiences and give back to the biosphere to ensure that it continues to thrive.

[Find out more about biosphere supporters](https://www.wrb.scot/join-us/biosphere-charter/our-supporters)

## The Wester Ross Biosphere by area

Each community within the biosphere has its own character. Explore the areas below to discover the different landscapes, stories and experiences across this corner of the Highlands.

[Gairloch](https://www.visitwester-ross.com/stay/gairloch/) – a scenic village combining coastal scenery and local culture. Visit Gairloch Museum, the community-led GALE Centre or spot marine wildlife on a boat trip.

[Ullapool](https://www.ullapool.com/) – a lively fishing village at the shores of Loch Broom and ‘gateway to the Outer Hebrides’.

[Kinlochewe](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/kinlochewe/kinlochewe/index.html) – this small village at the shores of Loch Torridon is surrounded by towering mountains, glistening lochs and stunning scenery.

[Plockton](https://visitplockton.com/) – this idyllic spot with its sheltered bays and crofting tradition is often described as the ‘Jewel of the Highlands’.

[Glenelg](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/glenelg/glenelg/index.html) – twinned with Mars, Glenelg offers unexpected stories. Arrive on the last seafaring turntable ferry, explore ancient Iron Age brochs, and drive across the Ratagan Pass with views towards the Five Sisters of Kintail.

![Ullapool Harbour](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2024/09/03/ullapool)

Ullapool

## Nearby regions

Find out more about the regions surrounding the Wester Ross Biosphere and extend your trip. From a few days exploring Inverness and Loch Ness to a week on the beautiful Isle of Skye or elsewhere in the Highlands, there is plenty more to discover nearby.

previousnext

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2022/12/07/inverness-cathedral)

### [Inverness](https://www.visitscotland.com/places-to-go/inverness)

Discover Inverness, our capital of the Highlands, with scenic riverside walks, historic sights and a warm local atmosphere.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2026/09/28/quiraing.jpg)

### [Isle of Skye](https://www.visitscotland.com/places-to-go/islands/isle-skye)

With rugged mountains, sweeping coastal views, rich clan history and unforgettable wildlife experiences, the ‘Misty Isle’ is sure to captivate you.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2026/09/28/loch-clair)

### [The Scottish Highlands](https://www.visitscotland.com/places-to-go/highlands)

Green valleys, vibrant culture, towering mountains, historic castles and peaceful lochs: the Highlands is the Scotland of your imagination.

## Plan your trip to Wester Ross Biosphere

The Wester Ross Biosphere is located in the northwest Highlands. Despite its remote location, it is still perfectly accessible to travel to and explore.

- Getting there
- Accessibility

### Getting there

Train

## Train

You can travel by train to Inverness from major destinations such as London, Glasgow, Edinburgh and Aberdeen. From Inverness, you can travel into the biosphere on the Kyle Line, with several stops along the way.

[Plan your journey by train in Scotland](https://www.visitscotland.com/planning/travel-in-scotland/train)

* * *

Driving

## Driving

Travelling by car is one of the easiest ways to explore the Wester Ross Biosphere. Some roads are single-track so allow extra time for your journey and be prepared to use passing places.

Car from Glasgow to Wester Ross Biosphere: 4 hours 15 minutes

Car from Edinburgh to Wester Ross Biosphere: 4 hours 15 minutes

Car from Inverness to Wester Ross Biosphere: 1 hour 15 minutes

[Find more information about driving in Scotland](https://www.visitscotland.com/planning/travel-in-scotland/driving-road-trips)

* * *

Bus and coach

## Bus and coach

Bus services connect destinations such as Gairloch, Ullapool, and Kyle of Lochalsh with Inverness. As services can be less frequent in rural areas, it is important to plan your journey in advance.

[Read more about travelling through Scotland by bus](https://www.visitscotland.com/planning/travel-in-scotland/bus-coach)

* * *

### Accessibility

Accessible attractions and visitor experiences can be found throughout the biosphere, helping more people discover its landscapes and history. Check for accessibility information with local providers when booking your stay. The charities [AccessAble](https://www.accessable.co.uk/) and [Euan’s Guide](https://www.euansguide.com/) provide more information to help you plan your accessible holiday or day out.

## FAQs

What is a biosphere?

### What is a biosphere?

[Biospheres](https://www.visitscotland.com/places-to-go/unesco/biospheres), or UNESCO Biosphere Reserves, are areas where both local communities and nature thrive. These areas have been designated as biospheres by UNESCO to highlight their commitment to sustainable development that enables not only the protection and restoration of valuable ecosystems but also the establishment of resilient communities and businesses.

* * *

When is the best time to visit the Wester Ross Biosphere?

### When is the best time to visit the Wester Ross Biosphere?

The biosphere offers something different in every season. Spring, summer and autumn are great for exploring the outdoors, with opportunities to experience the landscapes, wildlife and rich biodiversity. Winter brings cooler temperatures and unpredictable weather but is a great time to experience the warm welcome of local communities, with ceilidhs, and other events taking place in local village halls. Clear nights reveal some of the darkest skies in Scotland and offer perfect stargazing opportunities.

* * *

How long should I stay in the Wester Ross Biosphere?

### How long should I stay in the Wester Ross Biosphere?

The biosphere rewards those who take their time so choose one or two locations as a base to fully explore this region over 3-5 days.

* * *

Where can I stay in the Wester Ross Biosphere?

### Where can I stay in the Wester Ross Biosphere?

Whether you are looking for a stay in a rustic cabin, a self-catering cottage, a cosy B&B or a lodge on a working estate, the Wester Ross Biosphere offers accommodation to suit every style and budget.

[Find your accommodation using the interactive map](https://www.wrb.scot/join-us/biosphere-charter/our-supporters)

* * *
